_note: Allied political calendar and leadership register. Added 2026-09-02 (operator-approved) after two failures of the same class: the UK changed prime minister on 2026-07-20 and the board carried no UK entry for six days, and Hungary changed government on 2026-05-09 and the board still carried nothing four months later. A 24-hour news sweep structurally cannot see a fact whose news cycle already closed — only a standing calendar can. Maintained by the daily planner; see 2-plan.md prep step 5b.

maintenance.cadence: Review every run. Re-verify any leader whose last_verified is more than 45 days old; that check is the whole point of this file.
maintenance.sourcing: Elections: an official electoral commission or a directory outlet. Leaders: a government primary (kormany.hu, elysee.fr, gov.uk) or two directory outlets. Wikipedia may locate a URL but is never the citation.

elections.stakes: NATO membership has broad cross-party consensus; the live question is the defence-spending trajectory, not alliance reversal.
elections.source: riksdagen.se / val.se (date); France 24 2026-09-14 (result, read in full)
elections.status: HELD 13 Sep — centre-left opposition 176 seats. Kristersson resigned 17 Sep. The new Riksdag convened 28 Sep; a prime-ministerial vote was reported as possible from 29 Sep (research return citing riksdagen.se — not read directly).

elections.stakes: Not a government election, but flagged by analysts as the first durability test of the sitting coalition.
elections.source: Candidate date 9 October 2026 from a research return citing volby.gov.cz, whose fetch redirected — NOT verified; needs a resolving electoral-commission page

elections.stakes: Direct control of Ukraine-aid appropriations and NATO-adjacent funding. The single highest-consequence vote in this window.
elections.note: HELD 3 Nov. Democrats won control of both chambers; at least 54 Senate seats per Al Jazeera (4 Nov, read). New Congress sits in January 2027.

elections.stakes: P5 nuclear power. Macron is term-limited out. Bears directly on European extended deterrence and EU-level Ukraine-aid unity.
elections.source: DATES NOT FETCH-VERIFIED — france24 403 on 2026-09-02. High confidence but does not clear the bar; re-verify at a French government primary.

elections.stakes: NATO member since 2023 with a 1,340 km Russian border; the eastern border has been closed since 2023 over instrumentalised migration.

elections.status: HELD — Tisza won; Magyar PM from 2026-05-09
elections.stakes: Reported to have removed the EU's most consistent veto on Ukraine funding and Russia sanctions. The board carried no Hungary entry at all until 2026-09-02.

elections.note: Scheduled 27 October; reaffirmed by Al Jazeera (27 Sep) reporting on the opposition's pre-election coordination. No early change announced.
elections.result: Final: Netanyahu bloc 53, Eisenkot camp 48, Arab parties 19; Likud 27 (Euronews 30 Oct; NYT 29 Oct). President Herzog to consult party leaders.

elections.stakes: The first State Duma election since the full-scale invasion, held over three days from 18 September and including voting in occupied Ukrainian territory. Not a competitive contest for control, but the occupied-territory voting is a formal annexation claim and the result sets the legislature that ratifies wartime measures.
elections.source: NPR 2026-09-19 (voting in seized areas); Kyiv Independent 2026-09-20; Foreign Policy 2026-09-18
elections.status: HELD 18-20 Sep — election commission count at 83.5% of precincts: United Russia 57.8% of the party list, leading in 208 of 225 districts (TASS, statement of record, 21 Sep). Voting also held in occupied Ukrainian territory.

elections.stakes: State contests that do not change the federal government, but are read as a test of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's standing after earlier far-right gains in the east. Germany is one of Ukraine's largest European backers and a unanimity vote in every EU sanctions renewal.
elections.status: HELD 20 Sep — final: AfD first in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania (~38%), Linke first in Berlin (25.7%); Merz called it a disaster (Euronews, 21 Sep). No federal change.

elections.stakes: Lula seeks re-election; he has accused Trump of meddling. A runoff, if needed, follows on 25 October. Brazil is a founding BRICS member.
elections.source: Al Jazeera 2026-10-05 (result and runoff date, read in full)
elections.status: HELD 4 Oct (first round) and 25 Oct (runoff) — Lula just over 51%, Flávio Bolsonaro 48% at 98.76% counted (Al Jazeera, read 26 Oct); Bolsonaro refuses to recognise the result.

elections.stakes: NATO and EU member; called by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez after parliament rejected his housing measures. His Socialist Party trails in polls, so a change of government in Madrid is possible.
Vučić's SNS against the student-led movement after a year of protests; Serbia balances EU candidacy and ties with Russia.
elections.status: HELD 25 Oct — Vučić conceded; CESID projection Student List 138 of 250 seats, SNS 104; turnout ~70%.

elections.stakes: NATO and EU member on the Black Sea. Iliana Iotova, described as favouring better Russia ties and backed by PM Radev's party, faces the pro-Western Andrey Gyurov.
elections.note: HELD 1 Nov. Central Election Commission declared Iliana Iotova elected with 57.6% to Andrey Gyurov's 39.5% (BTA, 3 Nov 2026, read).

watchlist: Any NATO / G7 / Quad / AUKUS member changing head of government by election, resignation, coalition collapse, succession or no-confidence vote.
Any allied government entering caretaker status or losing a confidence vote.
Any state where an anti-NATO or pro-Russia party enters government or leads polling.
